key_insight: A frozen, general-purpose LLM can propose low-energy quantum circuit parameters for structured problems, but performs worse than Adam optimization on general random Hamiltonians.
engineering_relevance: LLM-generated circuit parameters enable independently verifiable energy estimates, making them more reliable engineering outputs than direct LLM energy predictions.
method: Generate complete circuit parameter vectors from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions.
Optionally refine parameters using iterative energy feedback.
Evaluate random Hamiltonians, structured parent Hamiltonians, molecular systems, and blind circuit interpretation.
evidence_signal: Evaluations found promising low-energy configurations for structured Hamiltonians, larger errors than Adam on general Hamiltonians, and generally limited gains from feedback.
watch_item: Direct LLM energy predictions can violate spectral lower bounds; independently evaluate generated circuits rather than trusting numerical predictions.
paper_title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
